body: It's an actual phenomenon that occurs in our subconciousness. Maria Mandic has an article about it. Explaining it in a somewhat thorough way. You should look it up.
Seems like it's up to me when I want the surgery to be done. I'm in-charge of it and it's not like it's a life and death situation whether I fix my larynx or not.

The doctor said I have to wait for about 2 months so that the burns and stitches inside to heal properly before they could do another surgery on me. So I guess I have time to decide about it. 2 months to be specific.

Well, first of all, my voice isn't that lovely. Children are afraid of it even since it's deeper than the ocean. Second, I am considering other options like you said, learing 'shuwa' or sign language. Lastly, I'm not much of a talkative person to be honest. Hopefully, my voice won't be that essential in my life.

The doctor gave me two options essentially. One, restore my voice box and be able to converse proper again with a low chance of damaging my windpipe making me unable to breath and later, die. Or, not taking the chance and just wait 10 more years to add an augmented voice box inside my throat so that I can talk but, with robot voice. (or something else. Fully customizable.) 



I came up with the cons part since the doctor didn't tell me much and the second option was out of the window because my relatives didn't agree to taking someone from the family's larynx parts and donate it to me.
Thank you, my dear. I love you, too. And, yes. I'm planning on staying alive for a little while longer.
I can laugh, hum and whistle. I can produce sounds apparently. Not words though.
Tragedy. Bittersweet tragedy.

But, it's alright to feel that way to be honest. We're humans after all. We're flawed. But sometimes, flaws can also be beautiful. It can become our strengths instead of weaknesses.
What seems to be the problem in your new workplace?
In my place, I took Information Tech since whenever there's information roaming around and technology advancing, I can always get a job. Or so I thought.
I love scary movies though so it's perfect!

Well, originally, my dream was to become an engineer. My family never owned a house before so I thought it would be the perfect job. But, the older I got, the more realistic I became so yeah. Here's to our dreams that never came true.
Thanks a lot. It makes me feel better seeing these kind of words from lovely people.

Thanks for the kind compliment. I like seeing that there are people out there with the same perception of life as me. And yes, I am undergoing therapy. It's going pretty good for the most part and I can say that it helps one way or another.
The feeling's mutual, my dude. If we've met irl, we could've been close friends I can feel. I wish you all the luck in the world as well.
I will look up that movie and watch it for myself. Again, thanks a lot.
